sections.title: Product Vision and User-Segment Map
sections.body: Rig Relay's GitHub integration must become the best GitHub operating layer for every developer segment. This is not a 'does the API work?' audit — it is a deep product, UX, UI, governance, technical-architecture, security, procurement, and implementation audit. GitHub integration is a flagship differentiator. The goal: make GitHub feel less like a fragmented web app and more like a governed, observable, adaptive developer operating surface.

subsections.title: Solo Developer
subsections.body: Pain points: too many browser tabs for issues/PRs/actions/security; no unified dashboard; GitHub CLI partial; context-switching between code editor and GitHub UI. Rig Relay opportunity: single cockpit for all repo activity; local-first evidence; governed mutations; no-surprise PR behavior. Required UX primitives: compact repo health chip, issue-to-mission one-click, PR status inline, action failure notification. Required permissions: read-only by default, write gated behind explicit approval. Governance: dry-run-first, human-in-the-loop mutations. Telemetry: feature adoption patterns, frustration-signal detection. Procurement: free for solo use, local-only. Differentiation: unified local cockpit replaces 4-5 browser tabs; agent-assisted issue triage; content-light evidence for every operation.

subsections.title: Open-Source Maintainer
subsections.body: Pain points: triage overload, spam PRs, security alert fatigue, contributor onboarding friction. Rig Relay opportunity: automated triage queue, code scanning alert prioritization, Dependabot batch update planning, contributor CLA/permission audit. Required UX: security queue with severity scoring, PR review packet with risk summary, stale issue detection. Permissions: read public repos freely; write gated for owned repos. Governance: explicit attribution on all generated content; no marketing in PRs/comments. Telemetry: community health metrics, response-time analytics. Differentiation: governed agent PRs that never pollute; transparent provenance; batch security alert remediation planning.

subsections.title: Small Team (2-15)
subsections.body: Pain points: inconsistent code review quality, missed security alerts, deployment coordination, knowledge silos. Rig Relay opportunity: team-shared cockpit projections, PR review packet standardization, security posture dashboard, release readiness panel. Required UX: team activity feed, review queue, branch protection health, deployment status. Permissions: team-scoped GitHub App install. Governance: team-level approval chains, audit trail for all agent actions. Telemetry: team velocity, review cycle time, security debt trend. Differentiation: replaces fragmented GH notifications with structured, prioritized, governed feed.

subsections.title: Startup Engineering Org (15-100)
subsections.body: Pain points: velocity vs. security tradeoffs, compliance readiness, multi-repo coordination, on-call noise. Rig Relay opportunity: multi-repo portfolio view, compliance posture dashboard, incident timeline reconstruction, enterprise procurement readiness. Required UX: org-level security posture, release readiness across repos, cost/rate-limit dashboard. Permissions: org-scoped GitHub App with least-privilege profiles. Governance: SOC2/ISO27001 evidence generation, change approval workflows. Telemetry: compliance posture trends, security debt velocity. Differentiation: startup can demonstrate enterprise-grade security posture without enterprise overhead.

subsections.title: Security-Conscious Enterprise
subsections.body: Pain points: GitHub Advanced Security cost, alert fatigue, compliance audit overhead, permission sprawl, provenance gaps. Rig Relay opportunity: governed security pipeline with content-light evidence, permission posture reporting, audit-log ingestion, least-privilege enforcement. Required UX: security posture panel, permission matrix viewer, audit event timeline, code scanning/secret scanning/Dependabot triage queue, branch protection compliance report. Permissions: read-only GitHub App default + explicit mutation approval. Governance: HMAC-SHA256 attestation signing, append-only JSONL evidence, replayable audit trail. Telemetry: opt-out by default, de-identified aggregation, no raw content leakage. Enterprise procurement: security questionnaire evidence pack, data residency mapping, rate-limit budgeting. Differentiation: content-light, auditable, replayable evidence that GitHub native audit log cannot match; governed agent behavior with no surprise mutation.

subsections.title: Massive Technology Corporation (1000+)
subsections.body: Pain points: GitHub Enterprise Cloud/Server fragmentation, multi-org governance, thousands of repos, compliance at scale, procurement complexity. Rig Relay opportunity: multi-org portfolio analytics, enterprise policy engine, fleet orchestration across orgs, centralized evidence store. Required UX: enterprise admin panel, org-level compliance dashboard, fleet-wide security posture, rate-limit budget across orgs. Permissions: enterprise-scoped GitHub App, repository allowlist/denylist. Governance: SSO/SAML/SCIM-adjacent planning, enterprise audit-log ingestion, data residency controls. Telemetry: aggregated, de-identified fleet analytics; no raw repo content. Procurement: security questionnaire, pen-test evidence, SOC2/ISO27001 mapping. Differentiation: unified governance across GitHub Enterprise Cloud + Server; portable evidence artifacts; fleet-wide agent orchestration.

subsections.title: Agency/Consultant Managing Many Repos
subsections.body: Pain points: context-switching across client repos, inconsistent security posture, billing/procurement complexity. Rig Relay opportunity: multi-client portfolio view, per-client permission boundaries, automated security scanning across all managed repos. Required UX: client-switching cockpit, per-client security dashboard, billing/procurement evidence pack. Permissions: per-client GitHub App installs with isolated auth. Governance: tenant-scoped evidence, cross-client data isolation. Differentiation: one cockpit for N clients; per-client governed agent lanes.

subsections.title: AI-Agent-Heavy Engineering Team
subsections.body: Pain points: agent-produced PR pollution, unclear authorship, surprise mutations, permission overreach, provenance gaps. Rig Relay opportunity: governed agent lanes with explicit permission boundaries, agent-produced evidence timeline, agent attribution and provenance, agent behavior audit. Required UX: agent activity feed, agent permission matrix, agent-produced PR queue with risk summary, agent governance dashboard. Permissions: per-agent permission scoping, agent-specific GitHub App token profiles. Governance: every agent action produces a receipt; agent mutations are blocked by default; human review required for remote mutations. Differentiation: Rig Relay is the only tool that governs agent GitHub access with content-light, auditable, replayable evidence.

subsections.title: Non-Expert Business Owner (Static Site)
subsections.body: Pain points: GitHub too technical, Pages deployment confusing, content updates require developer help. Rig Relay opportunity: governed static site editing with preview, one-click deploy, content-light evidence of changes. Required UX: simple content editor, preview panel, deploy button, change history. Permissions: limited to Pages/content scope. Differentiation: makes GitHub Pages accessible to non-developers without exposing raw GitHub complexity.

sections.title: Current Implementation Inventory
sections.body: Factual inventory of the current GitHub integration across 37 Python modules, 37 scripts, 73+ schemas, 82+ governance artifacts, and 70+ test files. The integration spans: provider models/auth, capabilities engine, security pipeline (intake → queue → remediation → patch → PR → post-PR lifecycle), surface audit/packets/preview, profile README maintenance, claims index, operating picture, code scanning PR mutation (dry-run, readiness, execution, transaction, chaos lab), live mutation (preflight, adapter, rehearsal), permission posture, carte blanche expansion (21 API surfaces, 17 mutation lanes), live auth (JWT, token exchange), fake auth (deterministic simulation), GitHub App onboarding, token management, maintenance scheduler, and redaction. All modules enforce content-light patterns with SHA256 hashing. Mutation is blocked by default; all writes require explicit flags and preflight verification. Two-tier boundary: FakeGitHubBoundary (deterministic) and RealGitHubBoundary (live httpx). Phase 2 (Security Lifecycle Program) complete with 10 slices and 239 passing tests. Phase 3 (Live Mutation Readiness) in progress with 4 additional slices; live mutation remains blocked.

sections.title: UX/UI Leadership Audit
sections.body: What 'industry-leading GitHub UX' means inside Rig Relay. The cockpit must provide governed, observable, content-light projections of GitHub activity — not a GitHub clone. Every UX surface must be permission-gated, content-light, and backed by auditable evidence artifacts. See companion artifact: github_integration_ux_surface_map_v1.v1.json for full UX surface specifications.

subsections.title: UX Principles
subsections.body: 1. Content-light: never display raw tokens, secrets, or private repo content. 2. Permission-transparent: every UI element shows what permission enables it. 3. Action-gated: mutations blocked by default; UI shows 'why blocked' with governance explainer. 4. Evidence-backed: every data point links to its source JSONL artifact. 5. Adaptive: UX degrades gracefully when telemetry is disabled. 6. Segment-aware: solo, team, startup, enterprise modes with appropriate complexity. 7. Human-review boundary: clear delineation between agent-observable and human-decision surfaces.

subsections.title: Current UX State
subsections.body: Current cockpit: chat-first console with widget panels for workspace state, fleet status, provider health, and Council. Desktop projection via WebSocket. GitHub integration surfaces in cockpit: provider health chip (operating picture), security posture (via projection), mission topology (spiderweb visualization). Static docs: github-app-integration-audit-v0.html, github-pages-artifact-site.html. Gaps: no dedicated GitHub operating picture dashboard; no PR intelligence panel; no issue-to-mission conversion UI; no code scanning triage queue UI; no secret scanning UI; no Dependabot UI; no Actions failure cockpit; no branch protection viewer; no release readiness panel; no multi-repo portfolio view; no enterprise admin panel.

sections.title: Governance and Trust Audit
sections.body: How Rig Relay avoids the trust failures that make developers hate AI GitHub tools. See companion artifact: github_integration_trust_governance_map_v1.v1.json for full per-requirement status, gap analysis, artifact evidence required, tests required, and UI disclosure required.

subsections.title: Current Trust Posture
subsections.body: Rig Relay's current architecture addresses most trust requirements by design: all mutations blocked by default; dry-run/rehearsal required before any remote operation; content-light evidence with SHA256 hashing; no raw tokens/secrets in artifacts; explicit permission posture; fake boundary for deterministic testing; receipt-backed operations; HMAC-SHA256 attestation signing. However, several gaps exist.

subsections.title: Trust Gaps
subsections.body: 1. No-surprise-remote-mutation: architecture blocks by default, but the live mutation adapter path needs additional sabotage tests. 2. No hidden co-author attribution: PR plan includes attribution gates, but actual PR creation not yet live-tested. 3. No PR pollution: patch preview and proposal are content-light, but actual PR body generation needs pollution-prevention tests. 4. No marketing in PRs/comments: current architecture doesn't generate PR content, so risk is theoretical. 5. No unreviewed generated comments: not implemented yet; needs explicit review gate when implemented. 6. No unexplained permission escalation: permission posture reporting exists, but UI disclosure is incomplete. 7. No raw prompt/completion leakage: content-light artifacts prevent this, but telemetry redaction needs audit. 8. No private repo content leakage into telemetry: SHA256 hashing prevents this, but telemetry bundle structure needs audit. 9. Clear authorship/provenance: claims index exists, but agent attribution in PRs not yet implemented. 10. Dry-run/rehearsal before remote mutation: implemented for code scanning PR pipeline, but not for other mutation paths. 11. Explicit human review boundary: architecture defines this, but UI doesn't yet enforce it. 12. Reversible mutations: not yet implemented. 13. Rate-limit safety: preflight checks exist, but programmatic budget enforcement missing. 14. Branch protection respect: addressed in PR plan gates, but not yet live-tested against real branch protection rules. 15. GitHub App permission transparency: permission posture report exists, but cockpit UI doesn't show it. 16. Audit trail for every GitHub API call: operating picture and receipts exist, but not unified into a single timeline.

sections.title: Trust Spine First Implementation Doctrine
sections.body: Current integration is deep in code-scanning/security lifecycle but skeletal across broader GitHub surfaces. The next implementation slice should harden provider trust substrate before adding more API families. GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1 is prerequisite infrastructure for later security signal expansion and cockpit UX. Broad ingestion before permission/rate-limit/webhook/dedup/leak-scan substrate would create fake-green dashboards. GitHub UX leadership depends on trustworthy data freshness, permission clarity, and evidence continuity — not just more widgets. Trust Spine v1 includes: live permission probe across all declared capability families, rate-limit budget enforcement with security/audit path prioritization, webhook HMAC-SHA256 signature verification with constant-time comparison, webhook idempotency and duplicate delivery suppression, polling-webhook deduplication with stable event identity, content-light leak scanning for GitHub-derived telemetry/projections (no secret fragments, no raw Actions logs, no raw diffs, no raw private repo content), cockpit permission transparency projection, and branch protection/ruleset preflight read model for mutation lanes.

sections.title: Data and Storage Architecture
sections.body: How GitHub-derived data should move through Rig Relay. See companion artifact: github_integration_storage_architecture_v1.v1.json for full Postgres table/view specifications, data flow stages, and artifact relationships.

subsections.title: Data Flow Design
subsections.body: GitHub API/webhook → provider packet → schema validation → content-light normalization → JSON/JSONL artifact → Postgres operational projection → DuckDB analytical projection → cockpit/static docs/API. Each stage: owner module, artifact path, schema, idempotency key (event_sha256 or resource_id+timestamp), hash/provenance fields (sha256, report_sha256, event_sha256), redaction rule (no raw tokens, no raw secrets, no source code in telemetry), retention rule (append-only JSONL forever; Postgres TTL-configurable; DuckDB disposable), replay rule (idempotent re-ingestion from JSONL source-of-truth), failure/quarantine behavior (quarantine directory for unparseable events).

subsections.title: Proposed Postgres Tables
subsections.body: 28 proposed tables/materialized views. See companion artifact for full column specifications, indexes, retention, tenant/repo/org keys, security class, and UI surfaces served. Key tables: github_installation, github_repository, github_repository_snapshot, github_permission_profile, github_provider_packet, github_api_call_receipt, github_webhook_event, github_issue, github_pull_request, github_pr_review_thread, github_check_run, github_workflow_run, github_code_scanning_alert, github_secret_scanning_alert, github_dependabot_alert, github_branch_protection_snapshot, github_ruleset_snapshot, github_release, github_pages_site, github_static_docs_projection, github_remediation_plan, github_remote_mutation_rehearsal, github_remote_mutation_receipt, github_rate_limit_budget, github_enterprise_audit_event.

subsections.title: Storage Principles
subsections.body: PostgreSQL: canonical enterprise operational substrate, not SQLite. JSON/JSONL/CSV: portable, inspectable, replayable evidence/source-of-truth layer. DuckDB: disposable analytical/read-side substrate. SQLite: forbidden. Content-light: SHA256 for all content-derived data; no raw tokens, secrets, private files. Idempotent: all ingestion replayable from JSONL source-of-truth. Tenant-scoped: all tables keyed by tenant_id, org_id, repo_id.

sections.title: Telemetry and Evidence Boundary Doctrine
sections.body: Product telemetry is default-on/opt-out. Remote telemetry contribution is separately controlled and enterprise-configurable. GitHub local operational evidence remains local-first and content-light. Enterprise audit/evidence continuity must continue even when product telemetry is disabled. Disabling product telemetry visibly degrades adaptive recommendations, UX optimization, agent-tool optimization, Ralph/orchestrator/subagent refinement, and product intelligence — but does not disable receipts, audit logs, permission probes, release-gate records, or governance evidence. GitHub-derived records must distinguish: public-safe (repo operating picture, aggregated security posture), private-local (raw alert details, branch names, repo metadata for private repos), sensitive metadata (permission scopes, token expiry, rate-limit consumption), secret-bearing (secret fragments — never stored), and forbidden raw content (source code, diffs, Actions logs bodies, PR comment bodies — never in telemetry, hashed only). Cockpit must distinguish and display: product_telemetry_disabled, remote_contribution_disabled, github_operational_observability_degraded, github_enterprise_evidence_unavailable, github_provider_rate_limited, and github_permission_probe_stale.

sections.title: Static Docs and Public Website Leadership
sections.body: How GitHub integration should feed the generated static site. Current static docs: deployed via GitHub Pages from docs/ on push to main. Generated via scripts/render_static_docs.py. Covers: repository operating picture, security posture summary, release readiness, evidence graph, governance history. Gaps and proposals below.

subsections.title: Public vs Private Split
subsections.body: Pages that can be public: repository operating picture (content-light), security posture summary (aggregated, no raw alerts), release readiness, evidence graph (with SHA256, no raw content), governance history, static docs, schema validation badges, trust-center/procurement pages. Pages that must remain local: raw alert details, private repo content, agent prompt/completion data, user-specific telemetry, rate-limit budget details, permission matrix with actual token scopes.

subsections.title: Proposed Public Pages
subsections.body: 1. Repository operating picture: aggregated health, recent activity, security posture score. 2. Security posture summary: high-level alert counts by severity, remediation progress. 3. Release readiness: version, test pass rate, evidence completeness. 4. Evidence graph: timestamp-indexed evidence timeline with SHA256 links. 5. Governance history: decision log with reasons (content-light). 6. Trust center: procurement evidence pack, security posture, compliance mapping. 7. OpenGraph/SEO: all public pages should have proper OG metadata. 8. Stale page detection: automated check via CI that compares rendered page timestamps against source artifacts.

subsections.title: GitHub Pages Deploy Flow
subsections.body: Current: pages.yml deploys docs/ on push to main. Enhancement: add pre-deploy validation (schema check, content-light scan, public/private split enforcement), post-deploy smoke test (verify pages render, OG metadata present, no private content leaked).

subsections.title: Rig Relay's Unique Position
subsections.body: No existing tool combines all of: governed agent behavior, content-light evidence, human-in-the-loop mutation control, multi-provider consultation (Council), fleet orchestration, desktop cockpit, static evidence site, and enterprise procurement readiness — in a single local-first product. GitHub-native tools (UI, CLI, Copilot, Advanced Security) excel at their individual functions but lack cross-surface governance, agent behavior control, and auditable evidence. Third-party tools (SonarQube, Semgrep, Qodana) are security-specialized but don't govern agent behavior or provide cockpit integration. CI dashboards show pipeline status but don't connect to agent governance. Backstage catalogs services but doesn't govern GitHub agent access. Rig Relay's wedge: governed, observable, evidence-backed GitHub operations that span security, development, and agent behavior — with explicit human review boundaries.

sections.title: Testing Strategy
sections.body: Tests that would fail if the GitHub seam leaks. See companion artifact: github_integration_test_strategy_v1.v1.json for full test specification with classifications (unit, contract, integration, E2E, real-artifact, adversarial, sabotage, concurrency, substrate).

subsections.title: Test Principles
subsections.body: Every trust boundary must have adversarial tests. Every mutation path must have sabotage tests. Every external API call must have contract tests with real captured fixtures. Every content-light guarantee must have redaction tests. Every rate-limit path must have budget tests. Every webhook path must have replay/idempotency tests. Every UX surface must have projection contract tests. Every public/private split must have leak-detection tests.

subsections.title: Current Test Coverage
subsections.body: 70+ GitHub-related test files across tests/integrations/, tests/governance/, tests/adversarial/, tests/release_gate/. Phase 2: 239 passing tests.
